_sources.esat: Bolton 1980, Mon. Wea. Rev. 108:1046, eq. 10: e_s(T) = 6.112 exp(17.67 T / (T + 243.5)) hPa (T in C); inverted for the dew point. Same formula as rust/boreal-sim hydrosphere_budget.rs esat.
_sources.dry_adiabat: Dry adiabatic lapse rate g/cp = 9.8 K/km (AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'dry-adiabatic lapse rate').
_sources.moist_adiabat: Saturated (pseudo-)adiabatic lapse rate G_m = g (1 + Lv r/(Rd T)) / (cp + Lv^2 r eps/(Rd T^2)) (AMS Glossary, 'moist-adiabatic lapse rate'). Lv 2.501e6 J/kg, Rd 287.04, cp 1004.6, eps 0.622.
_sources.environment: U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (NOAA-S/T 76-1562): 6.5 K/km to the tropopause at 11 km; pressure scale height RT/g ~ 8.4 km at 288 K.
_sources.vapour: Vapour falls off with height on a scale height of 2 km (rust/boreal-sim hydrosphere_budget.rs VAPOUR_SCALE_HEIGHT; Weaver & Ramanathan 1995, J. Geophys. Res. 100:11585).
_sources.ice_phase: Mixed-phase split of cloud condensate by temperature, ECMWF IFS Documentation Cy47r1 Part IV (Physical Processes) ch. 7: liquid fraction ((T - T_ice)/(T0 - T_ice))^2 between T0 = 0 C and T_ice = -23 C, all ice below [verify exponent and T_ice against the current cycle]. Below about -38 C droplets freeze homogeneously regardless (Pruppacher & Klett 1997, Microphysics of Clouds and Precipitation, ch. 7).
_sources.ice_optics: Cloud optical depth per unit condensate path is tau = 3 W / (2 rho r_e) (Stephens 1978, J. Atmos. Sci. 35:2123), so at equal water an ice layer is thinner by (rho_w r_liq) / (rho_ice r_ice). Liquid r_e ~10 um (Han et al. 1994, J. Climate 7:465); ice r_e ~30 um for midlatitude cirrus [verify against a cirrus r_e climatology]; ice density 917 kg/m3.
_sources.anvil: A deep convective tower stops rising at its equilibrium (zero-buoyancy) level and its outflow spreads sideways there as a glaciated anvil a kilometre or two deep, far wider than the updraught (Houze 2014, Cloud Dynamics 2nd ed., ch. 8; Yuter & Houze 1995, Mon. Wea. Rev. 123:1941). Only towers deep enough to glaciate (cumulonimbus, several km) form one. Depth, minimum tower depth and spread radius here are [game calibration] for the 32 km local box.
_sources.melting_layer: Snow falling below the 0 C level melts over a layer a few hundred metres deep, so the snow level sits about 300 m (1000 ft) below the freezing level (AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'snow level' and 'melting layer'; Lumb 1961, Q. J. R. Meteorol. Soc. 87:437) [verify depth]. Warm-rain clouds with no ice above them give rain whatever the surface.
_sources.entrainment: A rising cloudy parcel mixes in surrounding air at a fractional rate eps, so its temperature relaxes toward the environment as dT/dz = -G_m - eps (T - T_env). Deep convection sits near eps ~ 0.2 /km, shallow cumulus near 1-2 /km (de Rooy et al. 2013, Q. J. R. Meteorol. Soc. 139:1). The deep-convection value is used so towers stay below the undiluted-parcel top [verify against the review table].
_sources.cape: Convective available potential energy CAPE = g * integral from the LFC to the equilibrium level of (T_v,parcel - T_v,env)/T_v,env dz (AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'convective available potential energy'; Emanuel 1994, Atmospheric Convection, ch. 6). Virtual temperature T_v = T (1 + (1/eps - 1) q - q_c) includes water-vapour buoyancy and condensate loading (Emanuel 1994 ch. 4; AMS Glossary, 'virtual temperature'). Typical values: under ~300 J/kg weak, 1000-2500 moderate, above ~3000 strong (Doswell 2001, Severe Convective Storms, AMS Meteor. Monogr. 28) [verify thresholds].
_sources.wMax: Parcel-theory maximum updraught w_max = sqrt(2 CAPE), from converting all CAPE to vertical kinetic energy (Holton & Hakim 2013, An Introduction to Dynamic Meteorology, 5th ed., sec. 9.x on parcel buoyancy; Emanuel 1994 ch. 6). Observed updraughts are usually well below this bound because of entrainment, water loading and pressure perturbations [verify section number].
_sources.overshoot: A tower arriving at its equilibrium level still moving upward at w overshoots into the stable layer above by about w / N, where N is the Brunt-Vaisala frequency (~0.02 /s in the lower stratosphere), giving the 1-2 km overshooting domes seen above strong anvils (Houze 2014, Cloud Dynamics 2nd ed., ch. 8; Wang 2003, J. Geophys. Res. 108(D6):4194) [verify]. w is taken as half the parcel bound wMax (updraught_frac), since real updraughts reach about half of it [game calibration].
_sources.optical_depth: Condensate path W = integral of rho_air q_c dz with rho_air = p/(Rd T); optical depth tau = 3 W / (2 rho r_e) per phase (Stephens 1978, J. Atmos. Sci. 35:2123), liquid at rho_w 1000 kg/m3 and r_e 10 um, ice at 917 kg/m3 and 30 um. Convective condensate is capped at the Kessler autoconversion threshold (qc_auto_kg_kg) so the path is the suspended cloud water after warm-rain fallout, not the adiabatic upper bound: a deep tower then reads a few kg/m2 and tau of order 10^2-10^3, matching observed cumulonimbus paths.
_sources.kessler: Kessler 1969, Meteor. Monogr. 32: the warm-rain autoconversion threshold qc0 ~ 1 g/kg above which cloud water converts to precipitation (same qc0 as src/core/weather.ts KESSLER). Suspended convective condensate in the column is capped there so water path and optical depth follow the retained cloud, not the undiluted adiabatic liquid-water content.
_sources.rh_crit: Sundqvist, Berge & Kristjansson 1989, Mon. Wea. Rev. 117:1641: layer cloud forms above a critical relative humidity of ~0.8 (the sim's update_clouds uses the same scheme).
_sources.precipitable_water: Precipitable water PW = integral of rho_air q dz (kg/m2, numerically mm of liquid) (AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'precipitable water'). Observed column values run from a few mm in polar winter to 50-60 mm in the humid tropics (Trenberth, Fasullo & Smith 2005, Climate Dynamics 24:741) [verify range]. With q falling on a 2 km scale height and density on ~8.4 km, PW is close to rho0 q0 / (1/Hq + 1/Hp).
_sources.espy_lcl: Espy's approximation for the lifting condensation level: about 125 m above the surface per 1 C of dew-point depression (AMS Glossary of Meteorology, 'lifting condensation level'). Local moisture heterogeneity shifts the dew point; the same 125 m/K maps that onto the per-cell base around the column LCL.
